question: What two main natural hormones do synthetic contraceptives mimic?
explanation: Hormonal contraceptives are manufactured using synthetic versions of the female hormones estrogen and progestin to regulate the reproductive cycle. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is the primary health care clinic often the best place to introduce family planning services?

options.A: It offers free surgical procedures for all community members
options.B: It requires clients to undergo advanced laboratory testing first
options.C: It is usually the closest and most trusted point of contact for local women
options.D: It is staffed exclusively by specialized gynecologists

explanation: PHC clinics are embedded within communities, making them accessible and familiar places for women to seek reproductive health counseling. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h1)

question: How does progestin specifically block sperm from meeting an egg?

options.A: By raising the core body temperature of the uterus
options.B: By opening the fallopian tubes to flush them out
options.C: By destroying sperm cells directly in the vagina
options.D: By making the cervical mucus thick and impenetrable

explanation: Progestin alters the consistency of cervical mucus, creating a thick barrier that stops sperm from swimming upward into the womb. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h2)

question: What happens in the body when ovulation is suppressed by hormonal contraceptives?

options.A: Eggs are permanently destroyed inside the follicles
options.B: No mature egg is released from the ovaries
options.C: The ovaries double in size to store extra hormones
options.D: The ovaries stop producing all blood supply

explanation: Suppressing the mid-cycle hormone surge prevents the rupture of the ovarian follicle, meaning no egg is released for fertilization. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the main difference between combined hormonal methods and progestin-only methods?

options.A: Progestin-only methods always require a minor surgical operation
options.B: Progestin-only methods must be injected every single day
options.C: Combined methods contain two hormones while progestin-only methods contain one
options.D: Combined methods can only be used by women who have never given birth

explanation: The key distinction lies in their formulation: combined methods use estrogen and progestin, whereas progestin-only methods rely solely on a progestin compound. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h3)

question: A breastfeeding mother comes to the clinic asking for a contraceptive method that will not reduce her breast milk supply. Which category should the midwife prioritize?
explanation: Estrogen can negatively impact lactation, so progestin-only options are recommended for breastfeeding mothers during the early postpartum period. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which hormone in combined contraceptives is primarily responsible for the increased risk of blood clots?
explanation: The estrogen component in combined hormonal methods increases the clotting factors in the blood, raising the risk of thromboembolism in vulnerable clients. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is it important to ask a client about severe migraine headaches before prescribing a combined oral contraceptive?

options.A: Hormone pills stop headache medication from working properly
options.B: Headaches cause women to forget to swallow their daily pills
options.C: Estrogen cures chronic migraines and might mask other illnesses
options.D: Migraines with aura combined with estrogen increase the risk of stroke

explanation: Women who experience migraines with aura have a significantly higher risk of ischemic stroke when exposed to exogenous estrogen. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h4)

question: How often is the standard injectable contraceptive DMPA usually administered?
explanation: DMPA injectables provide contraceptive coverage for 12 weeks, requiring clients to return to the clinic four times a year for scheduled injections. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why do progestin-only pills require such strict adherence to the daily schedule compared to combined pills?

options.A: They contain a very large amount of hormone that causes toxicity if delayed
options.B: They dissolve in the stomach acid if not taken at sunrise
options.C: They wear off quickly, and missing a dose by just a few hours lowers protection
options.D: They only work if swallowed with warm herbal tea

explanation: Minipills have a short duration of action in the body and rely on daily consistency to maintain thick cervical mucus. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h5)

question: What do categories mean in the WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraception?

options.A: They tell the midwife how much the contraceptive commodity costs to buy
options.B: They indicate how safe a method is for a client with a specific medical condition
options.C: They grade the educational level of the woman seeking family planning
options.D: They measure the physical weight and height of the female client

explanation: The WHO MEC categories guide clinicians on whether a contraceptive method is safe or poses health risks for women with various medical conditions. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h6)

question: A 35-year-old woman who smokes 20 cigarettes a day requests a combined oral contraceptive pill. According to safety guidelines, what should the midwife do?

options.A: Prescribe the pill immediately after checking her blood pressure
options.B: Insist she undergo a pelvic examination before making a decision
options.C: Deny the combined pill and recommend a progestin-only method instead
options.D: Give her a two-year supply to reduce her clinic visits

explanation: Women over 35 who smoke heavily face a high risk of cardiovascular complications with estrogen, making progestin-only methods the safer choice. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following is a very common side effect of progestin-only contraceptives that often worries new users?

options.B: Complete hair loss on the head

explanation: Irregular spotting, unpredictable bleeding, or complete cessation of menses are normal and harmless side effects of progestin-only contraceptives. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h7)

question: What is the best way to handle a client who believes that contraceptive implants will travel around inside her body?

options.A: Perform a major surgical operation to show her the muscles
options.B: Refuse to give her the implant until she stops asking questions
options.C: Gently explain the anatomy of the arm and reassure her using accurate information
options.D: Tell her she is foolish for believing local stories from her community

explanation: Respectful counseling and clear education help dispel myths without shaming the client for fears rooted in community misinformation. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of good family planning counseling in primary care?

options.A: To force every young woman to accept a long-acting implant
options.B: To make sure the clinic meets its monthly distribution quotas
options.C: To convince clients that natural methods never work
options.D: To help the client choose and comfortably continue a method that fits her life

explanation: Counseling empowers clients to make informed, voluntary decisions and provides them with the support needed to stick with their chosen method. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h8)

question: Why should a midwife encourage a client to return to the clinic if she experiences side effects instead of just stopping her method?

options.A: To prove that the client was using the contraceptive incorrectly
options.B: To collect a penalty fee for missing her scheduled appointment
options.C: To force her to use a permanent surgical sterilization method
options.D: To offer support, discuss management, or switch methods safely

explanation: Open communication prevents unassisted discontinuation and helps clients find a solution or alternative method before an unintended pregnancy occurs. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T3#BMP126_U2_T3_h8)
